module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjectures associated with A109909

$a(n)$ = number of primes of the form $k(n-k)-1$.

*References:*
- [A109909](https://oeis.org/A109909)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA109909

/--
$a(n)$ is the number of primes of the form $k(n-k)-1$.
This counts the number of distinct prime values in the set $\{k(n-k)-1 | 1 \le k < n\}$.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.Ico 1 n).image (fun k => k * (n - k) - 1)
  |>.filter Nat.Prime
  |>.card

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 2 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : a 5 = 2 := by decide

/--
Conjecture: $a(n) > 0$ for $n > 3$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture : ∀ n > 3, a n > 0 := by
  sorry

end OeisA109909

reformulations.difference: Lean forms the distinct image over 1 ≤ k < n, rather than using the half-range 1 ≤ k ≤ floor(n/2) employed for the same prime form in OEIS's cross-reference A109908.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The expression k(n−k)−1 is invariant under k ↦ n−k, so the full-range and half-range images coincide. It is injective on the half-range, making the distinct-value count equal to the number of prime-producing half-range indices. Both natural-number subtractions agree with integer arithmetic on the permitted indices. The scratch file proves equality of the counts for every n and the corresponding equivalence of the positivity conjectures, without using the conjecture.

sources_consulted: OEIS A109909, read through the official data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A109/A109909.seq
OEIS A109908, including its half-range Maple and PARI algorithms: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A109/A109908.seq
DataCite bibliographic metadata for Niu–Zhang, On Two Conjectures of A. Murthy (2024): https://api.datacite.org/dois/10.13140/RG.2.2.16430.11848
review.notes: Checked the definition and all six theorems. All 93 published OEIS terms match by Lean evaluation; the five numerical tests agree with the source. Boundary checks give a(0)=a(1)=a(2)=a(3)=0, and the conjecture correctly begins at n=4. The quantified assertion matches OEIS's 'Conjecture: a(n) > 0 for n > 3' exactly. OEIS reports verification through 10^9 and no resolution. Experiments and equivalence proofs are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, which compiles successfully. The OEIS website was browser-challenged, so its official data mirror was used. The linked Niu–Zhang ResearchGate preprint was also inaccessible; only its bibliographic metadata was available, and no claim about its contents is made.
